create.name: Dr. Chris Germer
create.bio:
Chris Germer is a clinical psychologist in Cambridge, Massachusetts, best known as co-creator, with Kristin Neff, of Mindful Self-Compassion (MSC), an eight-week course for the general public that began in 2010 and is now taught in more than thirty languages. His own practice goes back to the 1970s, when he spent years travelling in India exploring yoga and meditation and first learned mindfulness at a hermitage in Sri Lanka. He later joined a Cambridge study group on meditation and therapy, and he teaches part-time on psychiatry at Harvard Medical School.

Self-compassion, as he teaches it, is mindfulness turned warm: meeting our own failures and hard moments with the kind of care we would offer a friend. MSC combines short talks, guided meditations such as affectionate breathing and loving-kindness phrases, and small everyday practices like the self-compassion break. With four senior MSC teachers he has more recently developed a follow-on course on working kindly with shame. He now spends most of his time leading workshops around the world and supporting MSC teachers. His books include The Mindful Path to Self-Compassion, The Mindful Self-Compassion Workbook, written with Neff, and Self-Compassion for Shame.

books.title: The Mindful Self-Compassion Workbook: A Proven Way to Accept Yourself, Build Inner Strength, and Thrive
books.author: Kristin Neff, Christopher Germer
books.description: A self-guided version of the eight-week MSC course, written with Kristin Neff. Each chapter pairs a short explanation with meditations and informal exercises a reader can work through alone.

books.title: The Mindful Path to Self-Compassion: Freeing Yourself from Destructive Thoughts and Emotions
books.author: Christopher Germer
books.description: His first book for general readers, written before MSC took shape. It explains why kindness toward ourselves matters and offers loving-kindness practices and everyday exercises for meeting hard feelings.

books.title: Self-Compassion for Shame: A Step-by-Step Guide to Inner Freedom
books.author: Christopher Germer
books.description: His 2026 book, drawn from the follow-on course he developed with senior MSC teachers. Short chapters explain what shame is and lead the reader through guided practices for meeting it with kindness.

books.title: Teaching the Mindful Self-Compassion Program: A Guide for Professionals
books.author: Christopher Germer, Kristin Neff
books.description: A detailed handbook for people training to teach MSC, written with Kristin Neff. It sets out the course session by session along with the thinking behind it.

free_resources.title: Affectionate Breathing (guided meditation)
free_resources.description: An 18-minute recorded meditation from his site that pairs attention to the breath with a gentle, kind attitude. It is one of the core practices in MSC, with written instructions alongside.

free_resources.title: Loving-Kindness for Ourselves (guided meditation)
free_resources.description: A free audio practice of offering warm wishes to oneself using simple repeated phrases, as taught in the MSC programme.

free_resources.title: Compassionate Friend (guided meditation)
free_resources.description: A 15-minute guided visualisation in which you imagine meeting a wise and caring presence and listen for what it has to say to you.

free_resources.title: Self-Compassion Break (guided meditation)
free_resources.description: A 13-minute version of a short practice you can use in any difficult moment: noticing the difficulty, remembering others feel it too, and offering yourself kindness.

He is a clinical psychologist with a small psychotherapy practice and a 'Therapy' section on his site; listed for Mindful Self-Compassion teaching and meditation, not therapy. Therapy-focused videos and books left out.
Shame: his current work centres on self-compassion for shame. I treated shame as an emotion, not a medical condition, and kept the book and the most-viewed talk; owner may judge it borderline.
Co-author overlap with Kristin Neff (rank 216): the MSC Workbook and Teaching the MSC Program are shared books.

No own paid offerings: his only listed event (8 Nov 2026 online workshop) has started by 10 Nov; MSC courses on his home page link to the Center for Mindful Self-Compassion and are taught by many teachers, so not listed as his.
